svg.text: Hub-and-spoke on Network Connectivity Center. Two regions: us-west4 (default) and us-west2.
One trust VPC across both regions, with a DMZ /23 per region.
Trust is a center spoke. Management is an edge spoke.
Not on the hub. No route to on-premises or other VPCs.
Only VPC on the hub with private services access (PSA).
Root peering zone to the DNS hub.
Managed services over Private Service Connect, not PSA.
Same layout as production, separate edge spoke.
Ranges come from the per-region pool.
Ranges come from the per-region pool.
HA VPN per region, two tunnels each, BGP. Advertises both regional /16s, each region's own /17s (affinity),
the restricted Google API VIP and the Cloud DNS forwarder range.
The routing VPC is a center spoke, so every spoke learns the on-premises routes and the hub's default route.
Trust is a center spoke and holds the DMZ. Management is an edge spoke with no default route of its own.
Cloud DNS hub: inbound forwarders for on-premises, one cloud zone, peering zones from each spoke.
Star topology: edge spokes reach each other only through on-premises, where the firewall decides.
Per-workload VPCs are vended from a reserved /18 per region and attached as edge spokes.
100.64.0.0/10 (GKE pods and services, proxy-only, PSC NAT) is excluded from the hub and never advertised.
